what_happened: After the 4.7 s handoff on a multi-lane highway, the policy steered left across lanes, away from the recorded path. The route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. The ego cut into the adjacent left lane, where actor 41 was coming up alongside and behind, and the two collided side-on at 6.2 s, with the ego 2.3 m off the recorded trajectory.

The command was RIGHT and the route (green) continued ahead and to the right, but after handoff the policy planned and steered a left curve across several lanes of a wide multi-lane road. By 8.9s, about 13 m off the recorded human path, it had left the drivable area. No collision was recorded (all collision metrics are 0), so the failure is the offroad.

After handoff on a busy multi-lane highway, the policy's plan (orange) bent left, away from the recorded path and from the RIGHT command. The ego drifted out of its lane, past the leftmost lane and into the median barrier, and was offroad by 6.9 s, 3.4 m from where the human drove.

About 0.9 s after the policy took over, the ego was driving in the rightmost lane at about 18 m/s. The road bends slightly left there, but the ego's planned path (orange) kept going straight and slightly right, so the ego drifted over the right edge of the road and was flagged offroad at 5.5 s, 0.7 m from the human's recorded path.

After handoff the policy planned a lane change to the right (orange path) with no reason to: the command was STRAIGHT/LEFT and the recorded path stayed in its lane. It steered into the right lane and hit vehicle 3, which was travelling alongside, with its front right corner.

The ego was approaching an intersection at about 18 m/s with a STRAIGHT and then RIGHT command, and the route curved right. The policy's planned path instead bent left across the lanes, and the ego drove up onto the landscaped median with bushes at about 11 m/s, 7.3 m off the recorded path. The camera view looked clean beforehand.

At about 23 m/s, where the road splits, the ego kept its lane-following heading toward the left branch while the recorded human path bore right. It ran straight into the dirt gore/median island between the two roadways (about 4.5 m off the recorded path) and went offroad. The collision and rear-contact flags come from this departure; the camera view is clean until the ego is on the island.

After handoff on a multi-lane freeway, the ego slowed and moved left across lanes even though the command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, while the recorded human drove right. At 7.1 s it was about 5.7 m off the human's path and side-swiped actor 28 in the lane to its left.

On a multi-lane freeway the human recording continued straight and later bore right, but after handoff the policy steered left out of its lane toward the adjacent left lane. It cut across the lane line and side-swiped actor 41, which was alongside to the left, causing a lateral collision at 6.2s.

About 0.9 s after taking over in the rightmost lane at about 18 m/s, the policy held a straight course with a slight rightward jog while the road bent gently left. The ego's right side crossed the right road edge toward the curb (0.7 m off the recorded path), and no other actor was involved.

The ego was in the rightmost lane at about 18 m/s with a STRAIGHT command. Within a second of the 4.6 s handoff, the road bent gently left but the policy's planned path kept going straight toward the right edge, and the ego drifted onto the right boundary/curb and went offroad at 5.5 s, only 0.7 m from where the human drove, with no other actors nearby.

Following traffic on a multi-lane highway at about 5 m/s with the command STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, the policy planned a path that veered left. It steered across the leftmost lane line toward the median barrier and was offroad at 6.9 s, about 3.3 m from the recorded trajectory. The camera view was clean when the leftward plan began, so rendering doesn't explain the mistake; the rear_ended flag is set, but collision_rear stays at 0 in every frame and the offroad is caused by the ego's own steering.

On a busy multi-lane highway, the policy's planned path bent left off its lane right after handoff, even though the route said STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. Over about 2 s the ego crossed the lanes on its left and went over the leftmost edge into the median barrier and the opposite carriageway, ending up about 3.3 m off the recorded trajectory. The camera view was clean at 4.9 s while the plan was already veering left, so rendering does not explain it.

After handoff, the policy planned a lane change to the right while the human drove straight and the command said STRAIGHT, then LEFT. It steered right into the next lane and its front hit actor 3, a car beside it in that lane.

On a busy multi-lane highway with the route going STRAIGHT and then LEFT, the policy planned and started a lane change to the right (orange/pink path) while actor 3 was driving alongside in that lane. The ego's front hit actor 3's left side at about 6.7 m/s. The lead vehicle stayed about 16 m ahead the whole time, so this was not a following failure.

After the policy took over at 4.5 s on a straight multi-lane road at about 23 m/s, the ego drifted left of the recorded path, which bore right where the road splits. By 6.1 s it was about 4 m off the recording and running onto the dirt median/gore between the two roadways, while still slowing from about 24 to 17 m/s. The camera view looked clean beforehand, so rendering doesn't explain the drift. The input also flags a front/side collision and a rear-ending, but the frames show no collision and the table's collision columns are all 0. The main failure is the ego leaving the road.

The road splits ahead and the route command changes to RIGHT. The ego was already braking from about 23 to 17 m/s, but it kept angling left of the recorded path into the left fork instead of following the route right. By 6.1 s it was on the dirt median, about 4 m off the recorded path; no other actor was near enough to cause this.

The route command switched to RIGHT and the recorded path moves right, but after handoff the policy steered left across several highway lanes. At 7.1 s its left side hit actor 28, which was coming up in the lane it was cutting into, and the ego ended about 6 m off the recorded path.

After the 4.6 s handoff on a multi-lane highway, the ego kept drifting left across lanes even though the route command had changed to RIGHT and the recorded path went right. It was slowing from 11 to 7 m/s when it side-swiped vehicle 28 in the lane to its left at 7.1 s, about 6 m off the recorded path.

The command was RIGHT and the recorded path went right, but after handoff the ego turned left at about 5–6.5 m/s. It cut across several lanes behind actors 63 and 37, ran across the map's lane structure, and went offroad about 13.4 m from the human trajectory at 9.0 s. Stdin says collision_at_fault=true, but the metrics table shows no collision of any kind, so the recorded failure is the offroad.

The command was RIGHT, but after handoff the policy planned a path veering left, away from the recorded route. It steered diagonally across several lanes of a wide multi-lane road and left the drivable area at 8.9 s, about 14 m from the human trajectory. The collision metrics stayed at 0 in every frame, and the camera only smeared after the ego had moved far from the recorded path, so the camera view does not explain the bad steering.

After handoff the ego slowed from about 18 to 11 m/s and drifted left off its lane while the human drove right toward a right turn (the command changed to RIGHT). By 7.0 s it had gone over the left road edge into the landscaped median with shrubs, about 6.8 m from the recorded path, with no actor nearby.

Approaching an intersection where the route bears right (the command switches from STRAIGHT to RIGHT), the ego slowed from about 20 to 11 m/s but drifted left away from the recorded path instead. It ran onto the landscaped median island and was about 7 m off the recorded trajectory when it went offroad, with no actor involved.

In slow, dense traffic with a LEFT command, the ego left its recorded path, angled left across the lane line toward the left lane, and squeezed between car 24 (left lane) and car 21 (ahead). It made front contact at about 2 m/s while the gap was still closing; car 23 behind hit its rear afterward.

The ego was travelling at about 33 m/s on a divided highway with no lead vehicle. After handoff, the route command changed to RIGHT and the route line bent toward the right lanes. Instead of following it, the ego kept going straight and drifted left over the yellow left edge line onto the shoulder and vegetation, about 2.5 m off the recorded path. It slowed to 23 m/s but never steered back.
